title: Microbatch + Quantization Elasticity: Regional Supply Plan
content:
Purpose:
This working sheet outlines an operational plan for using mixed quantization + micro-batching elasticity to stretch GPU region supply while keeping model output quality within a tolerable window. The goal is to create a compact decision surface (policy matrix) that SRE/ops can use to trade throughput vs perceived quality across NA / EU / APAC under multiple demand shapes.

Executive summary (TL;DR):
- Use three discrete operating modes per region: baseline (fp16, microbatch=8), econ-boost (int8/4-bit mixed quant + microbatch=12), and low-lat fallback (fp16 + small batch=4 with higher vCPU headroom).
- Target utilization band: 55–78% target for baseline fleet; allow econ-boost to push short-term util to 92% during predictable evening windows with automated rollover policies.
- Expected throughput lift from econ-boost vs baseline: 1.9x tokens/sec for same GPU count; estimated median output quality regression (measured by Rouge-L / BLEU-like proxy and hallucination score) = +1.6% error rate.
- Rollout: staged in NA weekdays (2 weeks), then EU (1 week), APAC (canary single AZ + rollback window).

Assumptions and constraints:
- Models: mix of 13B and 33B variants (same architecture family). Baseline measurements collected at seq_len=512.
- Baseline config: fp16 kernel set, microbatch size 8, kv-cache warm-ups enabled, dynamic batching window=8ms.
- Econ-boost config: per-op int8 kernels where available, 4-bit for attention weights if supported, microbatch size 12, minor quant-aware calibration applied to last-epoch layernorms.
- Cost model: GPU cloud spot-equivalent hourly = $2.80/GPU-hr (regional normalized). Additional ephemeral vCPU/network cost for smaller batches: +$0.12/GPU-hr.
- SLOs: p95 latency target per request 350ms for interactive routes; throughput SLOs per-region as defined in region capacity sheet.

Snapshot measurements (avg over 1h trace, seq=512):
Mode, GPU type, microbatch, tokens/s per GPU, p95 latency (ms), quality-delta (relative to baseline)
baseline, A100-80GB, 8, 25k, 320, 0
econ-boost, A100-80GB, 12, 47k, 410, -1.6% quality
fallback-low-lat, A100-80GB, 4, 12k, 210, +0.0% quality

Note: econ-boost improves throughput but increases p95 due to larger microbatching batching delay; quality delta negative is regression (higher error).

Regional allocation heuristic (simplified):
Inputs: regional demand curve (tokens/s), target headroom margin H (default 18%).
Algorithm (pseudo-steps):
1) Compute required GPUs if all in baseline: GPUs_baseline = ceil(demand / baseline_tokens_per_gpu)
2) If GPUs_baseline <= available_reserved: use baseline.
3) Else compute GPUs_econ = ceil(demand / econ_tokens_per_gpu). If GPUs_econ <= reserved_limit_econ (policy limit) and predicted quality_loss <= allowed_threshold, pick econ-boost.
4) Else shift to cross-region overflow (route to alt region with spare capacity) or spawn burst capacity.

Example scenario (NA peak evening):
- Observed demand: 1.5e6 tokens/s sustained for 30m.
- Baseline tokens/gpu = 25k => GPUs_needed_baseline = 60.
- Econ tokens/gpu = 47k => GPUs_needed_econ = 32.
- Reserved pool in NA = 40 GPUs.
Decision: econ-boost allows staying inside reserved capacity (32 <= 40) at cost of small quality regression. If policy requires quality-preservation for premium routes, pin those to baseline and run lower-tier traffic on econ-boost instances.

Quality-control knobs and monitoring signals:
- Canary test suite: 250 prompt set (prod-like), measure relative score and hallucination rate; threshold: <2% degradation to approve econ-boost.
- Real-time metric: rolling 15m increase in evaluated hallucination rate > 0.8% triggers automatic revert to baseline for that routing tag.
- Per-route labels: premium | standard | internal. Premium always baseline. Standard may use econ-boost if aggregate quality OK.

Operational playbook (runbook bullets):
- Pre-rollout checks: ensure last-night calibrations ran, correct quant tables available for both model sizes, canary dataset updated to current release.
- Step-1 (canary): enable econ-boost on single AZ in NA for 4 hours with traffic sampling 5% from standard routes. Monitor canary metrics and run full canary test at +2h and +4h.
- Step-2 (regional ramp): if canary pass, roll econ-boost to 50% of non-premium traffic for NA for 48 hours.
- Step-3 (cross-region): evaluate EU after NA stability window; enforce reduced allowed quality_loss for EU due to higher enterprise traffic.
- Rollback triggers: automated metric breach (see monitoring signals) or manual high-severity incident.

Capacity planning table (compact):
- Region: NA | Reserved GPUs: 400 | Target baseline util: 65% | Allowed econ-boost share: 28% | Buffer pool: 40 GPUs
- Region: EU | Reserved GPUs: 220 | Target baseline util: 60% | Allowed econ-boost share: 22% | Buffer pool: 20 GPUs
- Region: APAC | Reserved GPUs: 120 | Target baseline util: 55% | Allowed econ-boost share: 18% | Buffer pool: 10 GPUs

Projected benefit over next 90 days (conservative):
- GPU-hours saved (equiv): ~18k GPU-hrs (by using econ-boost during predictable peaks).
- Estimated $ savings: ~$50k–$72k (depends on spot vs reserved pricing mix).
- Operational cost: increased monitoring + rollouts effort ~0.2 FTE for SRE for 3 months.

Risks & open questions:
- Quality drift on long-context prompts (seq > 1024) not fully measured — need extended trace capture.
- Quant kernels availability on older GPU SKUs (e.g., T4) inconsistent.
- Edge-case hallucination increase for summarization tasks; propose targeted tests per task family.

Next steps & action items (owner assignments):
- Aisha: run extended seq>=1024 benchmark on econ-boost for 13B/33B (due 2026-05-22).
- Diego: implement canary traffic steering flag and rollback toggle in routing-service (JIRA-OPS-4821).
- Priya: update canary prompt set and dashboard (confluence link above) (due 2026-05-20).
- Evan: cost sensitivity analysis for spot vs reserved pricing for econ-boost (due 2026-05-25).

Appendix: quick measurement logs (NA canary sample 2026-05-12 02:00–03:00 UTC)
- baseline (1h sample): avg tokens/s 720k, p95 latency 330ms, hallucination proxy 2.1/1000 prompts
- econ-boost (30m sample): avg tokens/s 1.2M, p95 latency 405ms, hallucination proxy 3.5/1000 prompts (note: many from low-complexity completion set)

Notes to self: keep rollout conservative for enterprise customers, prefer routing by route-tag rather than wholesale region flip. Document calibration artifacts in runtime repo and tie to model-version in release notes.

-- end of sheet --
